comment: Defaults for `geo prune`. History is evidence, so the defaults are generous: a year, a hundred runs per project, ten megabytes of records. The point of pruning is that an append-only file does not grow without bound, not that old audits are worthless. Stored pages have their own budget, a hundred megabytes a project: a page is stored once, but one that changes on every run is stored every run, and a measured page ran to 62 KB gzipped. Past the budget the oldest runs lose their pages first and keep their records. No stored page is deleted within a day of being written or reused, because an audit stores its pages before it appends the record that names them.
